_: THE source of truth for OpenDrone colour. Screen and physical. Nothing else restates these values: every other repo reads this file or links to it. If you are about to type a hex into another repo's README, you are about to create the drift this file exists to prevent.

screen._: sRGB, for anything emissive. These are exact and must not be 'adjusted for the background'.

gold.use: Drone, the mark, the accent. Every ground, no exceptions.
gold.note: Hue 80.25 sitting exactly on the sRGB chroma ceiling. Chroma FALLS above this lightness, so there is no brighter gold and lightening it only turns it chalky.
gold.warning: 1.62:1 on light is deliberate. Fine for the mark and the wordmark, which are exempt from contrast rules. Never body copy, never a focus ring, never a control boundary on a light ground.

surface_light.use: brand off-white ground, not pure white

incutec_teal.use: incutec accent. Only ever inside the incutec logotype.

retired._: Do not reintroduce. Listed so a grep for an old value lands here.
retired.#c89d2e: old light gold. Hue drifted 6 degrees toward green, which is why it read brown on white.
retired.#fdb600: old dark gold. Superseded by #ffb700, which it differs from by dOKLab 0.004.
retired.#b8922e: undocumented, lived in email and CSS fallbacks
retired.#dab040: old hover. Superseded by the oklab mix, #ffc559.
retired.#C08C10: undocumented, lived in the docs colour table

physical._: For anything reflective: print, anodised aluminium, powder coat, woven goods, plastics. The screen hex is NOT a physical spec and must never be handed to a supplier.

master.note: Below the ~1.0 just-noticeable-difference threshold, so it reads as the same gold as the screen colour. This chip is the physical master. Every substrate is matched to IT, never to the hex and never to another substrate.

physical.why_not_cmyk: #ffb700 sits outside CMYK gamut at C 0.171. Process colour physically cannot reproduce it; it lands duller and browner, which is the exact failure the screen colour was changed to fix. Use the spot ink.

tolerance.measurement: spectrophotometer, D65 illuminant, 10 degree observer, measured on the production substrate and not on a proof

print_coated.note: Specify spot. Do not let a printer substitute a CMYK build.

print_uncoated.note: The same ink prints duller on uncoated stock. Check a drawdown before signing off; a brighter number may be needed to LOOK like 1235 C.

print_digital_no_spot.note: A known compromise for short digital runs. It will be duller. Never use it for packaging or anything placed next to a spot-printed piece.

anodised_aluminium.note: Gold anodising is a dye process with real batch variation. Require a signed master panel from the anodiser and keep it; re-approve every new batch against that panel, not against a fan guide.

powder_coat.note: Do not order by RAL number. The nearest RAL golds are visibly off; specify the Pantone match and a master panel.

woven_and_textile.spec: nearest Pantone TCX to 1235 C, chosen on a physical fan
woven_and_textile.note: TCX is a different library on cotton, and no numeric conversion between Solid Coated and TCX is reliable. Take the 1235 C chip to a TCX fan under D65 and pick by eye, then record the TCX number HERE once chosen.

plastics.note: Opaque only. Translucent parts shift with wall thickness, so approve on a part at production thickness.

physical.open: The TCX number for woven goods has not been chosen yet. Nobody has held a fan against the master chip.

consumers._: Repos that read or mirror these values. Update this list when another one appears.
consumers.OpenDrone-Brand: tools/generate.py reads screen.gold from this file
consumers.OpenDrone-Web: app/styles/app.css --color-gold, the only gold literal in the site
